paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: a promise is only as good as the doing. The Gadites and Reubenites asked for good land, and Moses was not about to hand it over for free. He reminded them what happens when people hold back while their brothers face the fight (Numbers 32:6). Then they promised, "every man will cross over to the battle before the LORD," and the whole deal hung on that one line (Numbers 32:27).

Now look at what Moses says about the stakes. "But if you do not do this, you will certainly sin against the LORD—and be assured that your sin will find you out." (Numbers 32:23) I think that line is for us, too, because a promise to God is never small, even when nobody is checking. And notice the other side of it: the Lord's anger back then was about people who "did not follow Me wholeheartedly," while Caleb and Joshua did (Numbers 32:11-12). Wholehearted is the thing that keeps showing up.

So what do you do with that, baker? Think about what you've told people you'd do, and what you've told God. Your own comfort is a fine thing to enjoy, but it's no reason to leave your brothers and sisters alone in the work. Keep your word, finish what you said, and then enjoy the pasture, because the one who is faithful to the end gets to settle in with a clear heart.
